item.title: Physicists Trace Sun's Magnetic Engine, 200k Kilometers Below Surface
item.description:
Credit: NASA In an analysis of nearly three decades of solar acoustic data, NJIT physicists report evidence that the solar dynamo — the magnetic engine powering the Sun’s 11-year cycles and eruptive events — operates nearly 200,000 kilometers beneath the Sun’s surface. Every eleven years, the Sun’s magnetic field flips. Across the tachocline, the Sun’s rotation changes abruptly, generating powerful shearing flows capable of powering the Sun’s magnetic fields.

itchingsphynx:

Magnetohydrodynamic fluids are so cool! The fundamental concept behind MHD is that magnetic fields can induce currents in a moving conductive fluid, which in turn polarizes the fluid and reciprocally changes the magnetic field itself. Thus, a self-generating dynamo.
